sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: In the contemporary hyper-connected digital economy, data has emerged as the premier currency of corporate growth and statecraft, turning data privacy into an urgent battleground for individual autonomy. The systematic extraction of consumer behavioral data by surveillance capitalism models has normalized deep telemetry collection, often without the informed or meaningful consent of users. Individuals navigate digital spaces under the illusion of privacy, while their profiles are continuously aggregated, analyzed, and monetized by hidden data brokers. These systemic vulnerabilities are further compounded by an escalating cybersecurity threat landscape, where state-sponsored threat actors and decentralized cyber-criminal cartels exploit architectural zero-day vulnerabilities in critical infrastructure. Legacy defensive paradigms that rely on perimeter security are utterly obsolete against advanced persistent threats and ransomware-as-a-service models. Protecting digital ecosystems requires a decisive transition toward zero-trust data architectures and robust regulatory frameworks like GDPR, which codify data minimization and the right to erasure. Ultimately, cybersecurity can no longer be relegated as an isolated IT concern; it is a core pillar of national security and fundamental human rights.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: The strategic trajectory of India’s planetary exploration missions, coordinated by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), represents a profound departure from the historically cost-prohibitive paradigms of Western space programs. By engineering highly optimized, frugal engineering models, India has successfully executed complex deep-space assignments, including the Chandrayaan and Mangalyaan portfolios, at a fraction of standard international expenditures. This disruptive approach relies on maximizing gravitational slingshot maneuvers, localized component indigenization, and multi-mission modular hardware architectures. However, ISRO's evolution is transitioning from a period of pure scientific prestige and low-cost exploration into a highly commercialized and strategic aerospace phase. The opening of the domestic space sector to private enterprises and startups creates an energetic commercial ecosystem capable of competing in the global satellite launch and space-bound data analytics markets. Yet, this rapid commercial acceleration brings major challenges, including managing low-Earth orbit debris congestion, securing continuous institutional funding for high-risk deep-space scientific research, and establishing clear domestic space regulatory laws. India's long-term challenge is to scale its commercial aerospace footprint without compromising the core scientific curiosity and public-good objectives that defined its foundational space philosophy.

opts: collecting and monetising consumer behavioural data, often without real consent

They cannot defend against advanced persistent threats and ransomware-as-a-service
They depend on the right to erasure

questions.q: Spot the error: “Neither the teacher nor the students was present.”
questions.why: With neither…nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'students': 'were'. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2026.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “obfuscate”:
questions.why: To obfuscate is to make unclear. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct preposition: “The doctor prescribed rest ____ a week.”
questions.why: A period of time takes 'for'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Change into passive voice: “The teacher praised the student.”
opts: The student was praised by the teacher.
The student has been praised by the teacher.
The teacher was praised by the student.
The student is praised by the teacher.
questions.why: Simple past becomes 'was praised'. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2026.

questions.q: Choose the one word for: “A medicine that prevents disease”
questions.why: Prophylactic means preventive. GPSC-style practice item.

Hindi Diwas (14 September) marks the day in 1949 when the Constituent Assembly adopted Hindi in Devanagari as the official language of the Union. This is in Article:

questions.q: Who was India's flag bearer at the closing ceremony of the 2026 Asian Games?
questions.why: She won the women's trap gold, India's first individual trap gold since 1978. Oct 2026.

questions.q: The International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction is observed on:
questions.why: 5 November is World Tsunami Awareness Day.

questions.q: At what percentage above cost must an article be marked to gain 8% after a 10% discount?
questions.why: 0.9 × M = 1.08 × C, so M = 1.2 × C: 20% above cost. GPSC CBRT, Dec 2023.

questions.q: The average age of 59 students is 18. Including the teacher, it rises by 3 months. What is the teacher's age?
In an x m race, Chaupat beats Popat by 18 m and Sarpat by 24 m; Popat beats Sarpat by 8 m. Find x.
questions.why: (x − 24)/(x − 18) = (x − 8)/x gives 2x = 144, so x = 72. GPSC CBRT, Nov 2023.

questions.q: Father, mother and son's ages sum to 70; the father is 6 times the son. When their total is 140, the father will be twice the son. How old is the mother?
questions.why: Total doubles after t = 70/3 years; 6S + t = 2(S + t) gives S = 35/6, F = 35, M = 70 − 35 − 35/6 ≈ 29 y 2 m. GPSC CBRT, Nov 2023.

questions.q: In a class of 100, 60% play cricket, 30% football and 10% both. How many play neither?
questions.why: At least one: 60 + 30 − 10 = 80; neither 20. GPSC CBRT, Nov 2023.

questions.q: According to Hahnemann, the physician should also be a preserver of health by knowing and removing:
opts: the exciting and maintaining causes of disease
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. §4 and the note to §7.

questions.q: Hahnemann's essay 'Aesculapius in the Balance' (1805) was:
opts: a critique of the medicine of his time
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. It questioned the certainty of medicine.

questions.q: Kent's scale of potencies for repeated prescribing in chronic cases runs:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Each potency used until it ceases to act, then the next higher.

questions.q: Dryness of all mucous membranes, constipation with no desire, and craving for indigestible things like chalk or raw rice suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Alumina: inactive rectum, abnormal cravings.

questions.q: Glandular swellings, slow mental development, and timidity in children and the elderly suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Baryta carb: dwarfish mental and physical development.

questions.q: Fear of downward motion, as when a baby cries when laid down or rocked downward, and aphthae in the mouth suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Borax: dread of downward motion.

questions.q: Cough with exhausting weakness of the chest, so weak that the patient cannot talk, and sweetish expectoration suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Stannum: great weakness of the chest, pains come and go gradually.

questions.q: Potencies are numbered by:
opts: the number of dilution-succussion steps carried out
the amount of medicine in the bottle
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. 30C is 30 centesimal steps.

questions.q: For the 50 millesimal potencies Hahnemann medicated very small globules, about the size of:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. 100 such globules weigh about one grain.

questions.q: The method of repertorisation that starts with a characteristic keynote and studies only the remedies under it is:
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Quick but risky if the keynote is not truly characteristic.

questions.q: In Kent's Repertory, sensations like 'as if a band around the head' are found under:
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Particular sensations are under the relevant body part.

questions.q: The spinal cord in adults usually ends at the level of:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Lumbar puncture is done below this level.

questions.q: The normal fasting blood glucose in adults is about:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. 100–125 mg/dL is impaired fasting glucose.

questions.q: The tumour marker raised in hepatocellular carcinoma is:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. PSA for prostate, CA-125 for ovary.

questions.q: Scrub typhus, seen in Goa and other states, is transmitted by:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Orientia tsutsugamushi; an eschar is a clue.

questions.q: Pain radiating from the loin to the groin, with haematuria, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Usually due to a stone.

questions.q: Renal colic, worse on the left, with pains radiating in all directions and bubbling sensations in the kidney, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Berberis: radiating pains, bubbling sensation.

questions.q: Constipation with ineffectual urging, irritability and oversensitivity in sedentary people who overuse stimulants calls for:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Nux: frequent ineffectual urging.

questions.q: Abnormal uterine bleeding is classified by FIGO using the acronym:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. PALM (structural: polyp, adenomyosis, leiomyoma, malignancy) and COEIN (non-structural).

questions.q: Delayed dentition, late closure of the fontanelles and a thin, emaciated child craving smoked meat call for:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Calc phos: slow bone growth and dentition; Chamomilla is for painful teething with irritability.

questions.q: A wound healing by 'first intention' is one that:
opts: heals with minimal scarring after clean surgical closure
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Secondary intention involves granulation and contraction.

questions.q: Acute osteomyelitis in children most commonly affects the:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Slow, looping metaphyseal blood flow favours bacterial settling (Staph. aureus).

questions.q: The term 'epidemic' means:
opts: a disease always present at low level
occurrence of a disease clearly in excess of normal expectancy in a community
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Endemic means constantly present; pandemic means worldwide.

questions.q: Datura poisoning presents with:
opts: convulsions with a bitter almond smell
dry mouth, dilated pupils, flushed skin and delirium
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Anticholinergic syndrome.

questions.q: Under Indian criminal law, consent for a medical procedure given by a child under 12 years is:
opts: not valid; consent of the parent or guardian is required
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. A child under 12 cannot give valid consent for acts done for his or her benefit.
